description:
FILED s450v (Opus round 9 agent V), from the #541 range probes.  PRE-EXISTING, and
present in BOTH the unconditional and the `if COND` spelling.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3):

    our @a; @a = (1,2,3,4);
    { local @a[1..2] = (7,8); print "in=@a\n"; }
    print "out=@a\n";
        perl  in=1 7 8 4   out=1 2 3 4
        PCL   in=8 2 3 4   out=1 2 3 4

CAUSE: `_subscript_key_groups` splits on COMMAS, so `1..2` is ONE key group and
`@key_cls == 1`.  `_process_local_declaration`'s element branch then takes the
"single element with initializer" arm and emits
`(p-local-array-elem-init @a (p-.. 1 2) (vector 7 8))` -- the -init macro has no
slice arm at all, so `(to-number <vector>)` is 0 and the whole slice collapses
onto index 0 with the LAST value.  The comma spelling `local @a[1,2] = (7,8)` is
right, because two key groups take the SLICE arm (tmp + nested opens +
`(p-setf (p-aslice ...) tmp)`).

SHAPE OF A FIX: `@key_cls == 1` is the wrong test -- it should be "one SCALAR
key".  A key group containing a `..` at top level is a SLICE and must take the
slice arm, whose `p-aslice` place already handles a vector index.  (The
no-initializer range spelling `local @a[1..2]` was fixed in s450v by dropping
`p-local-array-slice`'s spurious `adjustable-array-p` test -- that macro's slice
arm is the model.)

BAR: the four spellings (range/list x with/without initializer) vs perl, plus
the `if COND` twin of each; rows in Pl/t/stmt-modifier-01.t Â§7 or local-elem-02.t.
subject: SILENT WRONG: `local @a[1..2] = (7,8)` treats the RANGE key group as ONE element and writes the last value to index 0 -- perl assigns 7,8 to elements 1,2
